claim: Cross-organism leave-one-organism-out (LOOCV) test of an ESM-2 650M + XGBoost essentiality predictor on the (Syn3A + M. pneumoniae) labeled dataset. Headline result: Syn3A held-out MCC = 0.1376 when training on M. pneumoniae's 593 ESM-2 embedded protein-coding genes and predicting Syn3A's 455 genes. Vs the v15 keyword-prior baseline of 0.5372, this is a delta of -0.3996 — well below the script's INTEGRATE band (>=0.55) and below its ENSEMBLE band (>=0.45). The script reports decision_band=FALSIFIED. The reverse direction (train Syn3A, test M. pneumoniae) gets MCC=0.1070. Both numbers are barely above chance (chance MCC ~ 0.0). Conclusion: ESM-2 embeddings + XGBoost do NOT transfer essentiality predictions across organisms at this data scale (~500 train rows per organism). The v15 detector's MCC=0.5372 on Syn3A specifically is achieved by biology-first priors (annotation-class + complex-assembly) that DO encode organism-specific information; sequence embeddings alone do not capture what makes those priors work cross-organism.
source_detail: Reproducible end-to-end via: (1) labels.csv with Syn3A (Breuer 2019) + M. pneumoniae (Lluch-Senar 2015) rows at memory_bank/data/multiorg_essentiality/labels.csv (1192 rows, commit 0ef09d3); (2) sequences.fasta with the corresponding 1048 protein sequences at memory_bank/data/multiorg_essentiality/sequences.fasta (commit e96f489); (3) ESM-2 650M embeddings parquet at cell_sim/features/cache/esm2_650M_multiorg.parquet (1048 x 1280, commit 716ffb3 from Colab T4 GPU run); (4) `python scripts/train_multiorg_xgboost.py --out outputs/multiorg_xgboost_loocv.json`. Full output JSON preserved at outputs/multiorg_xgboost_loocv.json with per-fold confusion matrices, top features, training wall times, and XGBoost hyperparameters.

value.mpne_coverage: 593 of 737 mpne loci have a sequence + embedding (80.5 percent); 144 orphans dropped silently in the join

caveats: Two-organism dataset only (Syn3A + M. pneumoniae). The original Session 20 plan called for five organisms (Syn3A, M. pneumoniae, M. genitalium, B. subtilis, E. coli). With more organisms, LOOCV would have more training data per held-out fold and the test would be more robust. The two-organism case is the smallest non-trivial cross-organism setup.

Class imbalance is severe and asymmetric across organisms: Syn3A is 84.2 percent essential (383/455); M. pneumoniae is 71.2 percent essential (422/593). XGBoost with default decision threshold 0.5 produces high precision but middling recall on Syn3A held-out (Pr=0.870, Re=0.786), and the inverse pattern on M. pneumoniae (Pr=0.724, Re=0.953). Decision threshold tuning could shift the trade-off but would not fix the fundamental MCC ceiling the embeddings impose.

ESM-2 650M is a generic protein language model. It encodes sequence context but not organism-specific gene context, regulatory architecture, complex membership, or pathway position. The v15 detector's biology-first priors (AnnotationClass + ComplexAssembly + iMB155 patches) ARE organism-specific in those exact ways. Cross-organism transfer fails not because cross-organism essentiality has no signal, but because ESM-2 embeddings discard the signal that v15 captures.

The 144 M. pneumoniae label orphans (loci in labels.csv but no sequence in the GenBank) drop silently. Recovering them (via Lluch-Senar Supplementary File S1 ZIP for smORFs, plus older NCBI annotations for the reannotation losses) would add ~20 percent more training data for the mpne fold but is unlikely to rescue the cross-organism MCC from the 0.10-0.14 floor.

v15 vs v18 are different methodologies, not directly comparable as 'better predictors'. v15 is a hand-engineered biology-first ensemble with full simulator state access; v18 is a statistical model on protein embeddings only. The v15 number (0.5372) was MEASURED on Syn3A's own training set (the same 455 genes used for v15's prior development); v18's 0.1376 is MEASURED on Syn3A genes the trainer never saw. v18's number is therefore a more conservative estimate of generalization. v15's number is a within-distribution upper bound on what biology-first priors can do for Syn3A specifically.

Decision band 'FALSIFIED' is the script's pre-registered category for MCC < 0.45 and reflects the project's Session 20 decision rule. The label is honest but accidentally connotes 'wrong'; the more careful reading is 'this approach does not lift over v15 at the data scale and feature set tested'. ESM-2 + XGBoost on protein sequences alone is a baseline; richer features (Pfam family, GO category, complex membership, expression level) could shift the result. None of those have been tested cross-organism in this measurement.
Single random seed (42). Multi-seed replicates would tighten the +/-0.02 noise floor; not run.
